newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg PM wants flexibility on key EMU figure.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg PM wants flexibility on key EMU figure.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minster Jean-Claude Juncker has underlined his opposition to a literal interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty budget deficit target for a single European currency.

"I'm vetoing this German interpretation that the treaty is saying 3.0 percent (deficit of GDP). It does, but it (the treaty) is rich as far as interpretation goes," Juncker, speaking in English, told reporters at an informal meeting on Wednesday night to launch the Luxembourg EU presidency.

"I'm in favour of a strict interpretation of the Treaty, but that is not the same as a strict interpretation of the criteria," said Juncker, whose country took over the rotating six-month EU presidency on July 1.
At a time when EU members Germany and France are in danger of missing the exact 3.0 percent deficit-to-GDP target, debate is raging over how to interpret the limit.
Juncker declined to specify what deficit-to-GDP ratio might be acceptable for France to join the first wave of countries taking part in a single currency.
"France has to bring its deficit for 1997 to as close as possible to 3.0 percent, but I don't think the final decision (for countries joining) will be on a 3.0 percent basis," he said.
French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Thursday that France's public deficit could be "significantly higher" than 3.0 percent.

The first members of the single currency, due to be launched on January 1, 1999, are expected to be chosen in April or May next year, under the British EU presidency, on the basis of their 1997 economic and budget performance.

Asked whether the Luxembourg presidency would consider how to deal with any market turbulence developing as more 1997 data became available, Juncker said "we have to be prepared for all events". But he added it made "no sense to add speculation to the debate" about how this would be done.
